prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone in Atlanta — the best choice depends on your exact needs, budget, system size, and the installer’s attention to correct sizing and workmanship. I can help you find the right company for your situation. First, here’s how to choose one and what to ask.

What to require from any contractor
- Proper Georgia license and current liability insurance.  
- EPA 608 certification for refrigerant handling and NATE-certified technicians (preferred).  
- Willingness to perform a Manual J load calculation (not just “one-size-fits-all” sizing).  
- Written, itemized estimate that separates equipment cost from labor and shows model numbers and SEER ratings.  
- Clear parts and labor warranties (ask for length and whether labor is transferable).  
- Local references and many recent positive reviews on Google/Yelp/Angi/BBB.  
- Permits and code-compliant work (they should pull permits if required).  
- Post-installation start-up and walkthrough, and a maintenance/inspection plan.

Questions to ask each contractor
1. Are you licensed and insured? Can I see proof?  
2. Will you perform a Manual J load calculation for my home?  
3. What make/model and SEER will you install, and what’s included (thermostat, new lines, pad, disconnect, drain, etc.)?  
4. What are parts and labor warranty lengths? Are any warranties transferable?  
5. Do you include permit pulling and city inspections?  
6. Who does the work — company employees or subcontractors? Are techs NATE-certified?  
7. How long will the installation take and when can you start?  
8. Do you offer financing or rebates? Any recommended utility or manufacturer rebates?  
9. Can you provide recent local references?  
10. Will you provide a written final invoice showing system serial numbers and start-up checklist?

Red flags
- Vague estimates (no model numbers, no line-item pricing).  
- Pressure to sign “today-only” deals.  
- No load calculation, or quoting by tonnage only without evaluating the house.  
- Very low bids with no warranty or unclear scope.  
- Requests for large cash-only down payments.

Ballpark cost (Atlanta, residential central AC replacement)
- Typical full system replacement: roughly $3,500–$8,000+ depending on size, SEER rating, and whether ductwork needs repair. High-efficiency or multi-zone systems cost more. Get three bids.

How I can help next
- If you tell me your ZIP code, house square footage, number of bedrooms, and approximate budget, I’ll:  
  - Tell you what size system range you should expect, and  
  - Help you evaluate any bids you receive (compare equipment, warranties, and scope) or draft an email to request quotes.

If you’d like, provide your ZIP code and a few details and I’ll help you shortlist and evaluate local installers.
